newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina seeks $2bln airport investment in 30 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Argentina seeks $2bln airport investment in 30 yrs.

text.p: The Argentine government on Thursday it expected the party that wins a 30-year concession to operate at least 28 Argentine aiports to invest $2.0 billion and pay the government an annual royalty of $40 million to $50 million.

Carlos Alfonso Ensinck, the government's coordinador of the National Airport System, said after President Carlos Menem signed the privatization decree that more of Argentina's 53 airports were likely to sign up before the tender on June 2.

"The level of interest shown by the provinces is huge," he said at a news conference. He said a single concession package would be defined June 2, the finalists chosen on August 28 and the tender awarded September 15.

More than 20 companies, from the United States, Italy, Britain, the Netherlands, France and Ireland, among other countries, have expressed interest in the privatization. The Union Bank of Switzerland is acting as adviser.
Argentine airport officials will travel to those countries to make details available to prospective investors.
